title: Wich AI and workflow for Unity Scripting
author: n3wdl
selftext:
Hey everyone, im currently trying to rebuild my offline battle system (its a structure an code mess and was only a gameplay test) 

I want to work with fishmmo(fishnet) as a core base for everything (to have  good networking fundamentals) and add my on world turn based party combat system

But i cant get Chatgpt to write me correct scripts for that (always buggy and never the fishmmo core structure correctly implemented) 

What is the workflow for you guys to achieve your goals on nearly production ready output of Ai?

(Sry english is not my native language)

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body:
Hi!  
I do AI TDD. The test is the documentation that the AI can lean against and ensure all is working. So it iterate on it own until al test is passing and if something breaks on one then the AI can troubleshoot in isolation. I write kind of recopies in an incremental way which drives the player avatars in a simulated way. The avatar gets encapsulated with a facade a test facade and a internal name space with a router. then all functionality lives inside as modules. the simulation is driven from inside and when mock is needed that also lives inside. I avoid interfaces as much as possible as that just adds complexity to the AI.

Then on top of that I have multiplayer guidelines on how we write multiplayer code, architecture guidelines. Most of the time I plan out what to build heavily before and then implement one system at a time. I know how to test it, how it works, how it's tested and so on.

The test are both single user and multi user. For multiuser test I use parrelsync. The default testing framework in Unity is well bad in my mind so I have rewritten a complete framework from scratch to handle this. I will not mention it here though as promotional post is not allowed.  
  
So with that said. try to make the AI agents load as little as possible. MCP agents have test support but that is in my experience to heavy cognitive wise. E.g. Coplay have a MCP that is capable of interfacing multiple clones at once but that get confusing for the agent when troubleshooting.

comments.author: ClueHappy324
comments.body:
I've had a lot of success with Claude Code. It gets infused with my game's design docs and the codebase itself. It becomes really easy to say things like "We've designed feature X but it hasn't yet been implemented. Treat this as a design session, and then we'll implement."

What I suspect you're missing is using a tool (i.e. a CLI, like Claude Code) that can read/write your disk. This is the secret sauce that will give your AI workflows innate context and authority to develop your project as you would yourself. If you're copy-pasting code between a web interface, it's missing all of the context. It cannot possibly give meaningful or correct code.
